item.title: Volunteers bring warmth to quake-hit Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
Abdu (1st L), Zhe Jiaxin (2nd L) and Alimjan Haliq (1st R) serve stir-fried rice noodles at a temporary shelter in Maru Township of Baqen County, Nagqu City, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, Oct. 26, 2026. In the wake of the earthquake that struck Baqen County on Oct. 22, several volunteers rushed to the quake-affected zone to serve hot meals, sending warmth to those affected who are facing high-altitude cold in late October. Among them was Alimjan Haliq, a volunteer from northwest China's Xinjiang. Knowing how difficult it is to cook at high altitude, he brought two pressure cookers with him all the way to the quake zone. Zhe Jiaxin, a young woman from Xinjiang, spent nearly 48 hours on a bumpy journey through multiple cities before finally reaching the epicenter. Abdu, who runs a Xinjiang restaurant in Lhasa, quickly rallied his friends, gathered supplies, and rushed to the disaster area. Their paths were different, but they converged on the snow-covered plateau for the same purpose. "There is strength in numbers," Alimjan Haliq said, voicing the thoughts of every volunteer. Upon arriving in the quake zone, the rows of tidy tents and prefab houses, ample supplies, and locals helping one another deeply moved the volunteers. Zhe Jiaxin said with emotion, "I want to do all I can to help the children here feel more comfortable." The unceasing cook fires and hot food from the volunteers did more than fill empty stomachs -- they let the affected people feel be cared and supported. item.title: China's wind and solar power capacity tops 2 billion kW
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
A drone photo taken on June 9, 2026 shows a wind farm and an energy storage power station in Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. By the end of September 2026, China's cumulative installed capacity of wind and solar power reached 2.01 billion kilowatts, the country's National Energy Administration announced on Monday. Of the total, solar power capacity stood at 1.31 billion kilowatts, up 16.5 percent year on year, while wind power capacity reached 700 million kilowatts, up 20.4 percent. item.title: Netanyahu's rival Eisenkot says ready to form government as exit polls show Israeli election deadlock
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
JERUSALEM, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot said Tuesday night that exit polls showing his bloc ahead of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's ruling coalition reflected a "complete lack of confidence" in Netanyahu's government, vowing to move swiftly to replace it, as the projections pointed to a parliamentary election deadlock. Exit polls by public broadcaster Kan and commercial TV Channel 13 projected 53 seats for Eisenkot's bloc against 50 for Netanyahu's, while Channel 12 gave Eisenkot's bloc 52 seats and Netanyahu's 50. Neither bloc reached the 61 seats needed for a majority. "If these are the final results, this is a victory for Israel's mainstream Zionist majority," Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, said in a statement. He pledged to act immediately to "implement the people's decision, replace Netanyahu's government and establish a Zionist government committed to military conscription as soon as possible." "The public has fired Netanyahu's government," said Yair Golan, leader of the center-left Democrats party, which supports the establishment of a Palestinian state. Yair Lapid, the current opposition head, said in a statement that the Netanyahu bloc has suffered "a crushing defeat" and "a total collapse." Arab-majority parties, the Joint List and the Muslim Ra'am party, were projected to win 17 to 18 seats in the 120-member Knesset or parliament, potentially holding the balance of power. Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot have ruled out forming a coalition with them. With no outright majority, the results point to potentially prolonged coalition negotiations and political instability. The exit polls are preliminary, with final official results expected in the coming days or even weeks. ■

item.title: Europeans take to streets over living costs, governance strains
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
* Protests across several European countries intensified pressure on governments already facing fiscal constraints and political divisions. * The current frustration has built up over years, with accumulated price increases coupled with renewed inflationary pressure. * The calendar of planned actions suggests that mobilization will continue through November, with disputes over budgets, wages and public services in focus. BRUSSELS, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- Waves of demonstrations, sometimes violent, across several European countries have shown mounting grievances and pent-up anger over inadequate housing, poor education and higher living costs. The latest protests, over the weekend, has intensified pressure on governments already facing fiscal constraints and political divisions. Further demonstrations and nationwide strikes have been called for November. AN AUTUMN OF DISCONTENT France saw another large turnout on Saturday, with the Interior Ministry counting 410,000 demonstrators nationwide and the CGT trade union estimating 800,000. Most marched peacefully, but clashes erupted in several cities. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said Monday that 1,435 people had been arrested. Around 50 shops were damaged, and retail activity fell about 80 percent, according to Alain Di Crescenzo, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of France, on Monday. Many shops closed as a precaution following violence on Oct. 17. "Every weekend, around 2 percent of annual turnover is lost," Crescenzo said. The protests pointed to falling purchasing power and worsening public services, following demonstrations by high school students in mid-September over teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and deteriorating school buildings. In Italy, demonstrations against rising living costs and increased military spending hit several cities. Clashes were reported in Rome, Bologna and Turin, with police using tear gas and water cannons during confrontations. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence, saying authorities must protect peaceful demonstrators as well as people working and living in the affected cities. The chaos has created additional pressure on businesses. The Italian business association Unimpresa put potential economic loss at 14.13 million euros (about 15.8 million U.S. dollars), from precautionary closures and protective measures across 11 cities. Housing remains a central grievance in Spain and Portugal, where protesters have occupied public squares to demand more affordable homes and stronger tenant protections. Thousands demonstrated again in Lisbon and Porto on Saturday, with smaller gatherings in Coimbra and other Portuguese cities. In Madrid, the issue has drawn people whose qualifications and employment have failed to secure an independent home. Claudia, who works in the documentary film industry, holds two bachelor's degrees but still lives with her parents. Asked about whether she could afford to rent a place of her own, she told Xinhua: "That's simply impossible." "Housing is a very serious problem, and I am directly affected by it," Paula, a trainee lawyer, said, explaining why she joined the protests. PRESSURES THAT FEED ONE ANOTHER The current frustration has built up over years, with accumulated price increases coupled with renewed inflationary pressure. Euro area annual inflation rose to 3.8 percent in September from 3.2 percent in August, according to Eurostat. Energy prices climbed 18.9 percent year-on-year, adding to pressure on household budgets. Price shocks have added on an already heavy burden for many. An analysis published on the European Central Bank's blog showed that euro area food prices remained around 30 percent above their end-2021 levels. Although wages had recovered relative to overall consumer prices, their purchasing power in terms of food remained below its pre-surge level. "Protests do not necessarily erupt at the peak of an inflationary shock, but rather afterward, when households realize that improving macroeconomic conditions are not accompanied by an actual decline in prices," Pablo Sanz, a professor at Spain's National University of Distance Education, told Xinhua. He Zhigao, an associate professor at the Institute of European Studies, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said economic difficulties were widening divisions between generations and among regions, increasing feelings of deprivation and abandonment among young people. Governments face growing demands to address those divisions while their capacity to spend is constrained, He said, stressing that weak growth and fiscal deficits make welfare commitments even harder to sustain. He said that economic and social dissatisfaction has been feeding polarization and challenging mainstream parties' ability to govern. Lenaik Dumont, president of Belgium's French-speaking students' federation FEF, said the organization had continued meeting political officials but had not received sufficient answers to its demands over education costs and study conditions. "There is a difference between being received and being heard," Dumont told Xinhua. "Dialogue is meaningful only if it allows decisions to change." "LONG WINTER" AHEAD The calendar of planned actions suggests that mobilization will continue through November, with disputes over budgets, wages and public services in focus. In France, Yellow Vest organizers have called for more demonstrations on Oct. 31, followed by nationwide strikes called by the CGT alongside other unions on Nov. 5. The unions are challenging the government's proposed 2027 budget choices and demanding higher wages and stronger public services. Spain's two major trade unions CCOO and UGT are preparing a nationwide strike on Nov. 11 over housing, precarious employment and purchasing power decline, while Italy's largest trade union confederation CGIL has announced a general strike for Nov. 20 over employment, wages, pensions, public healthcare and social rights. In Belgium, the FEF plans an education mobilization on Nov. 17. Major unions have also called for a demonstration in Brussels on Nov. 23, while the General Labor Federation of Belgium (FGTB) has threatened a possible general strike that week if the government's budget decisions cross its stated red lines. Governments are responding. After French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu met student representatives on Monday, the French government announced measures including replacing the university admissions platform Parcoursup by the start of the 2028 academic year, opening 15,000 additional higher education places and funding improvements to school and university buildings. In Portugal, a proposed rental reform aims to encourage housing supply, but tenant groups fear that its provisions will increase their insecurity. Sanz, the professor at Spain's National University of Distance Education, warned that replacing a government alone could not resolve persistent housing shortages, weak productivity and age-related fiscal pressures. Lasting solutions require consensus extending beyond a single electoral term, he said. Gregoire Roos of Chatham House said that France's violence was giving competing political forces new opportunities to mobilize anger against a weakened center. He said that further political fragmentation in France and Germany would undermine Europe's resilience. In a commentary on Friday, Michael Froman, president of the U.S. Council on Foreign Relations, urged Europe to tackle the underlying problems. "For its own sake as well as ours, Europe needs to address the structural weaknesses that are fueling both the protests and the geopolitical dependencies," Froman wrote. "Until they get their houses in order, we are all in for a long winter." ■ (Video reporter: Deng Chimin, Huang Xiaodi, Sun Xinjing, Cheng Chao, Yang Yating, Ren Yaoting, Leonardo Lombroso, Michele Novaga; Video editors: Liu Xiaorui, Wei Yin, Yu Jiaming, Zhang Yueyuan, Zhang Yucheng, Li Qin)

item.title: Why the CPC puts people's well-being at the heart of self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- In northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, eligible residents can receive certain forms of medical assistance and other support without submitting an application. Government departments share the information needed to provide the benefits. The provincial bodies responsible for disciplinary inspection helped drive the change. They prompted civil affairs departments to build a data-sharing network connecting 33 departments and institutions, enabling 12 frequently used assistance services to be provided without applications. The initiative offers a concrete example of how the self-supervision of the Communist Party of China (CPC) improve public services and help ensure that benefits reach those who most need them. Earning public trust through tangible improvements in people's lives is a defining feature of the CPC's full and rigorous self-governance, which is high on the agenda of the fifth plenary session of its 20th Central Committee. The key meeting, which opened Monday in Beijing, is considering a draft decision of the CPC Central Committee on major issues concerning strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance. COMMITMENT TO THE PEOPLE The CPC constitution commits the Party to serving the people, and states that it has no special interests of its own apart from those of the working class and the broadest possible majority of the people. Without seeking self-interest, the CPC can keep its spirit of thorough self-reform, and by swiftly detecting and resolving its own problems, the Party can prevent any interest group, power group or privileged stratum from preying on or corrupting its members. Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, has led an unprecedented anti-corruption campaign since 2012, driven by a determination to "offend a few thousand rather than fail 1.4 billion." The campaign has targeted corrupt officials at both high and low levels. Gyula Thurmer, president of the Hungarian Workers' Party, said serving the interests of the people is a central principle of the CPC. He added that the Party's anti-corruption efforts have achieved significant results, strengthening internal discipline and helping implement major economic and social development programs. SAFEGUARDING PEOPLE'S INTERESTS Xi has called on Party members to bear in mind that "benefiting the people is their greatest political achievement." An official review of work in 2025 reported that disciplinary and supervisory bodies nationwide investigated 967,000 cases of misconduct and corruption affecting people's daily lives, returning or helping recover about 77.6 billion yuan (11.5 billion U.S. dollars) in money and property to the public. Faruk Boric, president of the Association of Friendship between China and Bosnia and Herzegovina, said China's efforts to pursue corrupt officials at both senior and lower levels send "a clear message that no official is above the rules, regardless of their position." He said China's experience offers important lessons in linking clean governance with people's well-being. Protecting public funds, he added, helps direct more resources toward health care, education and other public services. BUILDING BETTER GOVERNANCE On several occasions, Xi has called for taking simultaneous, coordinated, and comprehensive steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity or desire to become corrupt. In his article on the Party's self-reform, Xi urged efforts to improve Party conduct, enforce discipline, and fight corruption, while integrating Party self-supervision with public oversight to deeply advance the Party's self-reform. Lyazid Benhami, a member of the Paris Association of French-Chinese Friendship, said rigorous Party self-governance can clarify officials' responsibilities, improve coordination and help sustain development programs. He highlighted China's emphasis on long-term planning, infrastructure, education and research, adding that the country has achieved a profound transformation regarding such priority areas and improved the well-being of its people. Those administrative strengths matter as China implements its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). In January, Xi urged efforts to confine power to an institutional cage in a more well-conceived and effective manner, and press ahead with the anti-corruption fight with a clearer understanding and stronger resolve, thus providing a strong guarantee for achieving the goals and tasks of the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Volker Tschapke, honorary president of Germany's Prussian Society, said the CPC's courage to "turn the blade inward" demonstrated a "moral strength that I truly admire." He stressed that rigorous Party self-governance ultimately serves the fundamental interests of the people. "I have seen with my own eyes what that has achieved: how villages have blossomed through targeted poverty alleviation, how rural areas have found new hope, how high-speed rail connects people and hearts," he said.■

item.title: China strongly deplores, gravely concerned about UK police's arbitrary, excessive law enforcement actions: foreign ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese side strongly deplores and is gravely concerned about the UK police's arbitrary and excessive law enforcement actions, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said Tuesday. Spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks at a daily media briefing in response to a related query about a recent security alert issued by the Chinese embassy in the UK, which advises Chinese citizens to be aware of recent practices in UK border checks. Recently, the Chinese Foreign Ministry and the Chinese embassy in the UK have received multiple reports of Chinese citizens being held and examined for extended hours by the UK police when entering and exiting the country, with their electronic devices including mobile phones seized, Guo said. He noted that China has lodged stern representations with the UK, and will take all necessary measures to keep Chinese citizens safe and protect their legitimate and lawful rights and interests. He also reminded Chinese citizens planning to travel to the UK to read carefully the embassy's alert to avoid any inconvenience or loss. ■

item.title: China's industrial profits post strong growth on electronics, high-tech gains
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- China's major industrial firms posted strong profit growth in the first nine months of 2026, driven by robust gains in the electronics industry and high-tech manufacturing, official data showed Tuesday. Profits of major industrial firms with an annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan (about 2.98 million U.S. dollars) rose 15.5 percent year on year during the January-September period, maintaining double-digit growth since the beginning of the year, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). In September alone, industrial profits at those firms increased 14.4 percent year on year, with the growth rate up 10.2 percentage points from August. NBS statistician Yu Weining attributed the overall profit growth to intensified macroeconomic policy support, steady industrial production and accelerated development of new quality productive forces. The electronics industry emerged as a key growth driver, with profits doubling from a year earlier and contributing 9.6 percentage points to the overall increase in industrial profits. Driven by demand for AI computing power and advanced memory technologies, profits in electronic specialty materials manufacturing surged 220 percent, while those in semiconductor discrete device manufacturing rose 51.7 percent. Meanwhile, profits in high-tech manufacturing surged 52 percent year on year, outpacing the overall industrial average by 36.5 percentage points. In the first three quarters, high-tech manufacturing accounted for 25.5 percent of the total profits generated by China's major industrial firms, up 6.2 percentage points from a year earlier. As high-end manufacturing continues to advance and new quality productive forces take shape at a faster pace, China's industrial sector is steadily shifting toward a more advanced and innovation-driven structure, Yu noted. Tuesday's data came as China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) highlights the development of a modern industrial system anchored by advanced manufacturing. The country will move to upgrade traditional sectors to the mid-to-high end of the value chain, nurture emerging industries, and make forward-looking plans for industries of the future, according to the development blueprint. Looking ahead, whether industrial profits can sustain robust growth will largely depend on how effectively the momentum in high-tech manufacturing spreads across broader industrial supply chains and whether stronger domestic demand can further support a recovery in profitability among midstream and downstream industries, analysts noted. Wen Bin, chief economist at China Minsheng Bank, said industrial profit growth could face near-term pressure before stabilizing in the fourth quarter, supported by recovering prices and continued strength in certain high-growth industries. He noted that the rollout of 800 billion yuan in new policy-based financial instruments, together with major infrastructure projects and urban renewal initiatives, could stimulate demand for electronic information products, electrical machinery, high-end equipment and certain raw materials. Meanwhile, continued global investment in AI infrastructure is expected to support China's electronics and equipment manufacturing supply chains, while exports of new energy vehicles, energy storage systems and power equipment are likely to remain resilient, Wen said. However, tightening global monetary conditions, uncertainty surrounding U.S. trade policies, geopolitical tensions and energy price fluctuations could weigh on external demand and corporate costs, he cautioned. ■

item.title: Xi extends condolences over death of Japan's former PM Yasuo Fukuda
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday extended condolences over the death of former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda to his family. In his message, Xi also extended sympathy to the family. Fukuda was a Japanese statesman known for his integrity and sense of responsibility, as well as a longtime friend of the Chinese people. He had long been committed to the China-Japan friendship and upheld a correct view of history, Xi said. During his tenure as prime minister, he signed the fourth political document between China and Japan with the Chinese side, setting out important principles for the development of bilateral relations, Xi said. Fukuda also served as chairman of the Boao Forum for Asia, playing an important role in promoting exchanges and cooperation in Asia, Xi said, noting that China will remember his contributions to China-Japan relations and Asia's development. Xi also expressed the hope that Fukuda's family would carry on his legacy and continue to work for China-Japan friendship. Xi expressed the hope that Japanese authorities would cherish the efforts of previous generations of statesmen, abide by the four political documents between China and Japan, and safeguard the political foundation of bilateral relations. ■

item.title: Xi congratulates Lula on re-election as Brazilian president
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday extended congratulations to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election as president of Brazil. In his congratulatory message, Xi said that President Lula has made important contributions to advancing China-Brazil relations. Xi said he and Lula have, in recent years, maintained close communication through various means and jointly guided the building of the China-Brazil community with a shared future for a more just world and a more sustainable planet to new progress. The global, strategic and long-term significance of the bilateral relationship has become increasingly prominent, making it a model of solidarity and cooperation among Global South countries, he said. Xi said that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Brazil relations and stands ready to work with President Lula to guide the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future to new heights, open up broader prospects for all-round strategic coordination between the two countries, and continuously enhance the well-being of the two peoples. Also on Tuesday, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng sent a congratulatory message to Geraldo Alckmin on his re-election as Brazil's vice president. ■
